blocks.text: The site grading design for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}} is under way, with our start set for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.start}}. This memo sets the assignments and the first tasks, so the project folder is in order from the beginning and no one waits on a hand-off that was never made.

The aim for the opening weeks is narrow. We open the lettered project folder, set up the sheet index and title blocks, and bring in the survey and the standard details, so that when design begins in earnest the file is already clean. Nothing here is design work yet; it is the groundwork that keeps the design orderly later.

The survey is the first thing we need. I will confirm with the client that we have the current one before we set any grade. Jason Jordan builds the existing-conditions base from it, and the grading plans start on top of that base. Until the base is right, nothing drawn over it can be trusted.

The job itself is straightforward in kind, if not in effort. We are grading a site, routing its drainage, and tying it to the roadway and utilities around it. The value is in getting the file and the coordination right at the start, because a set that is coordinated as it is drawn stays orderly through to issue.

items: Linda Nguyen: the grading plans, the project folder, and title-block and revision control across the set.
Jason Jordan: the existing-conditions base, the roadway and site base sheets, the border sheets, and the standard details, each confirmed current before we build on it.
Mark Barrett: logs the executed agreement when it comes back by fax, scans it on the flatbed, and files it in the job folder with the drawings it belongs to.
Debra Vasquez, Vice President of Finance, is our point of contact at the client; approvals and questions on their side route through her.

blocks.text: A note on the file itself. Every sheet is matched to the memorandum that governs it, and revisions are clouded and logged as they are made. That discipline is what lets us pull the current sheet in a hurry when the client calls, so please keep to it from the first print.

Coordination with the client runs through Debra Vasquez. When we need a decision or a document from their side, one of us asks her rather than several of us asking around, so the requests stay in order and nothing is asked twice.

items: 1. Open the lettered project folder and file the executed agreement once Mark Barrett has scanned it.
2. Linda Nguyen sets up the sheet index and the title blocks for the grading set.
3. Jason Jordan brings in the base survey, builds the existing-conditions base, and confirms the standard details are the current issue.
4. Confirm the kickoff and site-walk date with Debra Vasquez at {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}}.

blocks.text: We will meet briefly each week to keep the set coordinated as it grows. Between meetings, flag anything that does not match, a contour, a callout, or a detail, so it is fixed while it is still small.

Once the folder is open and the survey is mounted, we will start preliminary grading. Bring anything that belongs in the file to me, and I will see it filed in the right place. If a task on this list is unclear, ask before you start it rather than after.
